rules_text:
Rules summary Setup Choose a board layout. One player has white stones, the other player has black. Gameplay To start, Black covers any space marked "2". From then on, starting with White, the players take turns. On your turn, cover up to X empty spaces marked "X". For example, you could cover any 3 empty spaces marked "3". End of Game The game ends when the board is full. The player with the largest contiguous group of stones wins. If tied, compare the players' second-largest groups, and so on, until you come to a pair which aren’t the same size. Whoever owns the larger wins. Note that a tie is impossible.

[Rating: 6/10] In this game you choose a number X, 1 through 6, and place your pieces on X of those X numbered spaces of your choosing. If there are fewer spaces left of that number, you just take what you can. The game is light and interesting. You want to make long chains, but also avoid letting your opponent cut off your access to part of the board. I thought it was better to choose larger numbers to put out more pieces, but I lost most of the inside board to my opponent when he cut me off from it. I still won though. I'm not sure how much replay value it has, but it is quick and easy to jump into.
